name: Taiwan Digital Nomad Visa (DNV) — Complete 2026 Guide
description: Complete guide to Taiwan's Digital Nomad Visa: income requirements by age, application via TECO, documents, Gold Card comparison, and FAQ. Updated for 2026.
tagline: Live in Taiwan, work remotely for a foreign employer
keyRequirement: Remote employment with a foreign company and annual income of USD 20,000+ (under 30) or USD 40,000+ (30 and over)
targetAudience: Remote workers employed by companies outside Taiwan
Freelancers and independent contractors with foreign clients
Digital nomads seeking a base in Asia

eligibility.label: Employment or contract work with a company outside Taiwan
eligibility.description: Applicants must demonstrate that their employer or primary clients are based outside Taiwan. Local employment in Taiwan is not permitted under this visa.

eligibility.label: Annual income of USD 20,000+ (under 30) or USD 40,000+ (30 and over)
eligibility.description: Published income thresholds differ by age. Proof of income from the previous year or current employment contract showing salary is required.

eligibility.label: Nationality from a visa-exempt country
eligibility.description: The published requirements specify that applicants must hold a passport from a country with visa-exempt entry to Taiwan.

eligibility.label: Valid health insurance covering the stay in Taiwan
eligibility.description: Private health insurance or travel insurance with medical coverage is required for the duration of the stay.

eligibility.label: No criminal record
eligibility.description: A criminal background check from the applicant's home country is required.

eligibilityQuestions.question: Are you currently employed by or contracted with a company based outside Taiwan?
eligibilityQuestions.helpText: The published requirements specify remote work for a foreign employer or client. Local employment in Taiwan is not permitted under this visa.
eligibilityQuestions.mismatchNote: The published requirements specify that the DNV is for remote workers employed outside Taiwan.

eligibilityQuestions.question: Does your annual income meet the published threshold (USD 20,000 if under 30, or USD 40,000 if 30 or over)?
eligibilityQuestions.helpText: Income thresholds are based on published requirements from the National Immigration Agency.
eligibilityQuestions.mismatchNote: The published income requirements must be met. The threshold depends on the applicant's age.

eligibilityQuestions.question: Do you hold a passport from a country that has visa-exempt entry to Taiwan?
eligibilityQuestions.helpText: Check the published visa-exempt country list on the Bureau of Consular Affairs (BOCA) website.
eligibilityQuestions.mismatchNote: The published requirements specify that applicants must be from a visa-exempt country.

duration.extension: Extendable once for an additional 6 months (total 1 year)

fees.application: Varies by nationality and TECO office (typically USD 50-160)
fees.notes: Published fee schedules are available at the issuing TECO office or BOCA website.

incomeRequirement.notes: Based on published requirements. Income from foreign employment or freelance contracts. Proof may include employment contracts, bank statements, or tax returns.

documents.name: Valid Passport

documents.name: Proof of Income

applicationSteps.title: Gather Required Documents
applicationSteps.description: Prepare all required documents including proof of remote employment, income verification, and criminal background check with TECO authentication.

applicationSteps.title: Apply at TECO Office
applicationSteps.description: Submit the application at the TECO (Taipei Economic and Cultural Office) with jurisdiction over your current location. TECO offices are organized by geographic region — check the BOCA website to find the office serving your area. Some TECO offices accept mail-in applications; processing times vary by location.

applicationSteps.title: Application Processing
applicationSteps.description: TECO forwards the application for review. Processing times vary by TECO office.

applicationSteps.title: Receive Visa and Enter Taiwan
applicationSteps.description: Collect the visa sticker in your passport from TECO. Enter Taiwan within the validity period indicated on the visa.

applicationSteps.title: Register with NIA (upon arrival)
applicationSteps.description: After arriving in Taiwan, register with the National Immigration Agency within the timeframe specified on the visa. This step is required for stays exceeding 90 days.

processingTime.notes: Processing times vary by TECO office. Community members report 2-6 weeks depending on location and completeness of documentation.

restrictions: Local employment in Taiwan is NOT permitted
Work must be for employers or clients based outside Taiwan
Starting a business in Taiwan is not permitted under this visa
workPermission.notes: The DNV permits remote work for foreign employers only. Any local employment in Taiwan requires a different visa type (such as a Work ARC or Gold Card).

faqs.question: Does time spent in Taiwan on the DNV count toward APRC (permanent residence)?
faqs.answer: Based on published regulations, the Digital Nomad Visa does NOT count toward the continuous residency requirement for APRC. This is a critical distinction from the Gold Card and Work ARC, which do count toward APRC residency.

faqs.question: Can DNV holders enroll in Taiwan's National Health Insurance (NHI)?
faqs.answer: Published NHI enrollment rules generally require an ARC and 6 months of continuous residence. DNV holders typically do not receive an ARC and should maintain private health insurance. Verify current rules with the National Health Insurance Administration.

faqs.question: Can the DNV be converted to a Gold Card or Work ARC?
faqs.answer: The DNV itself does not convert directly. However, a DNV holder may apply separately for a Gold Card (online) or a Work ARC (through an employer). A change of visa status may require exiting and re-entering Taiwan.

faqs.question: What happens if the foreign employer terminates the remote work arrangement?
faqs.answer: The published visa conditions require ongoing remote employment with a foreign employer. If employment ends, the visa conditions may no longer be met. Contact the National Immigration Agency for guidance on the specific situation.

faqs.question: Are freelancers with multiple foreign clients permitted?
faqs.answer: Based on published requirements, freelancers working for clients outside Taiwan are generally covered, provided they meet the income threshold and can demonstrate that all work is for foreign entities.

faqs.question: How does the DNV compare to the Gold Card?
faqs.answer: The DNV and Gold Card serve different purposes. The DNV is for remote workers employed by foreign companies (no local work allowed), valid for up to 1 year, and does NOT count toward permanent residency. The Gold Card is for professionals with specialized skills, allows local employment and business creation, is valid for 1-3 years, and counts toward APRC residency. The Gold Card also provides potential tax benefits for qualifying salary. Refer to the published comparison for full details.

faqs.question: What are the tax implications of staying in Taiwan on the DNV?
faqs.answer: According to published Taiwan tax law, individuals staying 183 days or more in a tax year are generally classified as tax residents. Tax residents pay income tax on Taiwan-sourced income. Whether remote work income from a foreign employer constitutes Taiwan-sourced income is a nuanced question — consult a licensed tax professional for specific guidance.

faqs.question: Can I open a bank account in Taiwan on the DNV?
faqs.answer: Opening a bank account in Taiwan generally requires an ARC (Alien Resident Certificate) or a Taiwan phone number. Since DNV holders may not receive an ARC, banking options may be limited. Community members report that some banks accept passport-based accounts with proof of local address. Online banking alternatives are commonly used by digital nomads.

faqs.question: Is the DNV renewable beyond 1 year?
faqs.answer: Based on published requirements, the DNV has a maximum duration of 1 year (6 months initial + 6-month extension). After the maximum period, holders must leave Taiwan or apply for a different visa type. The Gold Card may be an option for those seeking longer-term residence.

tecoRouting.description: The Digital Nomad Visa must be applied for at the TECO (Taipei Economic and Cultural Office) with jurisdiction over the applicant's location. TECO offices are organized by geographic region.
tecoRouting.notes: Each TECO has jurisdiction over a specific geographic area. Apply at the TECO serving your current country or region of residence. Some TECO offices accept mail-in applications. Processing times vary by office.

taxImplications.notes: According to published Taiwan tax law, individuals who stay in Taiwan for 183 days or more in a tax year are generally classified as tax residents. Tax residents are subject to Taiwan income tax on Taiwan-sourced income. Foreign-sourced income may also be subject to the Basic Income Tax (最低稅負制) for residents with overseas income exceeding NTD 1M. DNV holders working remotely for foreign employers should determine whether their income constitutes Taiwan-sourced income. Consult a licensed tax professional for specific guidance.
